technical.clientSecretHandling: Server-side only. The client secret is sent in the code exchange and every refresh request, and it is the HMAC key for verifying the callback. No PKCE.

refreshTokens.expiry: 90 days from issue (refresh_token_expires_in 7776000); can end sooner once rotated
refreshTokens.notes: Only issued for expiring offline tokens (send expiring=1 at code exchange). Every refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token; the old refresh token stays usable only until the new one is used, a new grant happens, 30 days pass since its first use, or its 90 days run out.

technical.accessTokenLifetime: Expiring offline token: 3600 seconds (1 hour). Online (per-user) token: 24 hours or until the staff member logs out. Non-expiring offline tokens last until uninstall but are no longer allowed for new public apps on the GraphQL Admin API.
redirectUriRules: redirect_uri must exactly match a redirect URL configured in the Dev Dashboard or in [auth] redirect_urls of shopify.app.toml
At least one redirect URL is required before the app is made public
Use HTTPS; whether http or localhost works isn't documented for the Admin API

scopes.name: read_orders
scopes.purpose: Read orders, but only those created in the last 60 days

scopes.name: read_all_orders
scopes.purpose: Optional. Extends read_orders to older orders; needs Shopify approval for Partner-organization apps and must be declared together with read_orders

scopes.name: Protected customer data (Level 1, plus Level 2 fields only if needed)
scopes.purpose: Not an OAuth scope but a separate access grant. Orders are protected customer data, so without it order queries return errors or redacted fields. Name, email, phone and address are each a separate Level 2 field request.

testModeLimits.text: Before approval, a public app can be installed and tested on development stores without review, including protected customer data. Real merchant stores reportedly see that the app is under review and can't install it.

configGotchas.text: You can't change the distribution method after you pick it, and you must pick one before you can request protected customer data, even for development stores. For many merchants, choose Public distribution.
Send expiring=1 at code exchange. New public apps can't use non-expiring offline tokens on the GraphQL Admin API.
Anchor the shop-domain regex at both ends, or a domain like shop.myshopify.com.attacker.example passes validation.
read_orders alone only reaches orders from the last 60 days.

stage1.summary: Self-serve: create the app in the Dev Dashboard, pick Public distribution, select protected customer data for development, then run the authorization code grant against a development store.

stage2.summary: Installing on more than one real merchant store needs Public distribution, which needs Shopify approval, even if the listing has limited visibility. Protected customer data access is reviewed too, and read_all_orders needs its own approval. Developers in 2026 report reviews taking weeks.

time.range: About 2 weeks to 1.5 months per submission; resubmitting goes to the back of the queue
time.startsWhen: when you submit the app on the App Store review page

stage1DoneWhen.text: POST https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/api/2026-10/graphql.json on your development store with header X-Shopify-Access-Token and the query { orders(first: 1) { edges { node { id } } } } returns data.orders with no errors entry (node ids look like gid://shopify/Order/...), and your token response included expires_in and a refresh_token.

blockedBy.how: Shopify must approve Public distribution before real merchant stores can install, reviews protected customer data access for public apps, and approves read_all_orders. It can reject or temporarily suspend repeat failures.
Each merchant installs the app on their own store and approves its scopes. Staff reportedly need the Manage and install apps and channels permission to do this.

You have to meet the Level 1 (and, for names, emails, phones or addresses, Level 2) data protection requirements, pick the right distribution method the first time, and pass the App Store requirements, including OAuth right after install.

profiles.bottomLine: A first token from a development store is a same-day job, once you've picked Public distribution and selected protected customer data. The real gate is App Store review: even an unlisted public app has to pass it before any real merchant can install, and 2026 reports put the wait at weeks.
topRisks: Public distribution is a one-way choice and needs review before real stores can install; 2026 waits run to weeks
Orders are protected customer data: without approval, order fields come back null with errors
read_orders only covers 60 days; older orders need a separate read_all_orders approval

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
instructions: Sign in at https://dev.shopify.com/dashboard/ with an account in a Partner organization. The Distribution card only appears for apps in a Partner organization, so don't create the app in a store's organization.

Under Apps in the left navigation, click Create app, then Start from Dev Dashboard. Shopify suggests this path for API-only apps with no UI in the admin; Shopify CLI is the recommended path for embedded apps.
Enter a name and click Create.

links.label: Create apps using the Dev Dashboard

steps.title: Set scopes and the redirect URL in a version, then release
instructions: Open the app's Versions page.
App URL: a non-embedded app can use the default https://shopify.dev/apps/default-app-home.
Scopes: add read_orders. Add read_all_orders only after Shopify approves it (Stage 2); declaring it earlier causes an app_access validation error.
Add your callback URL as a redirect URL, exactly as your code will send it. Use HTTPS; whether http or localhost works for the Admin API isn't documented.
Click Release. Scopes and redirect URLs change only when you release a new version (or deploy with Shopify CLI from [access_scopes] and [auth] redirect_urls in shopify.app.toml).

links.label: Create apps using the Dev Dashboard

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and client secret
instructions: In the app, open App settings and find the Credentials card.
Copy the Client ID and reveal and copy the client secret. Keep the secret on your server or in a secret manager: you need it for the code exchange, every refresh and HMAC checks.

links.label: Create apps using the Dev Dashboard

steps.title: Choose Public distribution
instructions: On the app's Home page, find the Distribution card and click Select distribution method.
Choose Public distribution and confirm. You can't change this later.
Custom distribution doesn't fit this intent: it covers one store, or stores in one Plus organization. A separate custom app per merchant to avoid review breaks the Partner Program Agreement.

steps.title: Select protected customer data for development
instructions: Orders are protected customer data, so even a development store won't return them until you select it.
In the Partner Dashboard, go to Apps, select the app and click API access requests in the sidebar.
Under Protected customer data access, click Request access, select Protected customer data, give your reasons and click Save.
Only if you need customer names, emails, phones or addresses, select those fields (Level 2) with reasons and click Save.
You don't need to submit for review while the app is installed only on development stores; access works there right away.

steps.title: Get a development store with test orders
instructions: Create a development store from the Dev Dashboard (dev stores are managed there now), or select one when installing.
Add at least one test order so the Stage 1 check has something to return. (How to create test orders wasn't researched.)

steps.title: Send the store owner to the per-shop authorize URL
instructions: Generate a random state nonce and store it.
Redirect to https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&scope=read_orders&redirect_uri=YOUR_URI&state=NONCE (comma-separate multiple scopes).
Don't add grant_options[]=per-user: it gives an online token tied to one staff member that expires within 24 hours. A backend reading orders needs the default offline token.
Sign in to the development store's admin and approve the install.

steps.title: Validate the callback
instructions: The callback carries code, hmac, shop, state and timestamp.
Check that state matches the nonce you stored.
HMAC: remove hmac, sort the remaining parameters alphabetically, join them as key=value pairs, compute HMAC-SHA256 with the client secret, hex-encode it and compare in constant time.
Check shop against ^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9\-]*\.myshopify\.com$, anchored at both ends.

steps.title: Exchange the code for an expiring offline token
instructions: POST to https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/access_token as application/x-www-form-urlencoded with client_id, client_secret, code and expiring=1.
Store access_token, scope, expires_in, refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in, keyed by shop.
Check that scope includes read_orders; Shopify may grant fewer scopes than you asked for.
Before expires_in (1 hour) runs out, POST to the same endpoint with client_id, client_secret, grant_type=refresh_token and refresh_token. Store both new tokens, since refresh tokens rotate.

steps.title: Check the token reads orders
instructions: POST https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/api/2026-10/graphql.json with header X-Shopify-Access-Token: ACCESS_TOKEN and the query { orders(first: 1) { edges { node { id } } } }.
Expect data.orders.edges with node ids like gid://shopify/Order/... and no errors entry. A 200 with an errors entry means protected customer data isn't set up for this app.

steps.title: Request read_all_orders if you need orders older than 60 days
instructions: In the Partner Dashboard, go to Apps, select the app and click API access requests.
On the Read all orders scope card, click Request access and describe the app and why it needs older orders.
After approval, add read_all_orders alongside read_orders and release a new version. Merchants then have to approve the new scope.

steps.title: Complete the data protection details
instructions: On the same protected customer data request, complete Data protection details and confirm that you meet the Level 1 requirements (and Level 2 if you selected name, email, phone or address fields).
Ask only for the fields you use: Shopify approves the minimum the app needs.
Do this before submitting the app, because you can't apply while the app is under review.

steps.title: Complete App Store registration ($19 one-time)
instructions: In the Partner Dashboard, go to Settings, then App Store registration, and click Register now.
Enter the account ownership details and any Associated Developer Accounts, add a payment method and click Register.
The fee applies even to unlisted public apps.

steps.title: Submit the app for review
instructions: Open the Shopify App Store review page and complete Configuration setup, Protected customer data and Automated checks for common errors, plus an emergency contact, app icon and compliance webhooks.
The review page also requires an App Store listing. That's needed even with limited visibility, and it's the only way to reach many merchants. Listing steps are out of scope here.
Make sure the app runs OAuth immediately after install and on reinstall, and that install starts from a Shopify-owned surface rather than asking merchants to type their shop domain.
Allow emails from noreply@shopify.com so you get review messages.

steps.title: Wait for the review outcome
instructions: No official timeline. Expect 18 days to 1.5 months; reviews were slower than usual in 2026.
Resubmitting moves the app to the back of the queue. Repeated failures or unanswered review emails can lead to a temporary suspension.

requirements.label: Reasons for protected customer data
requirements.detail: The request asks why you need protected customer data and, separately, each Level 2 field (name, email, phone, address).
requirements.howToPrepare: Map each order field your product reads to a feature, and leave out customer contact fields you don't need.

requirements.label: Level 1 data protection practices
requirements.detail: Data minimization, telling merchants what you process and why, purpose limits, respecting consent and opt-outs, privacy agreements with merchants, retention periods, and encryption at rest and in transit.
requirements.howToPrepare: Write down a retention policy and merchant privacy terms, and confirm encryption before you attest.

requirements.label: Level 2 security practices (only with name, email, phone or address)
requirements.detail: Encrypted backups, separate test and production data, data loss prevention, limited staff access, strong staff passwords, access logs and an incident response policy.
requirements.howToPrepare: Document each control. Shopify may ask for a detailed data protection review later.

requirements.label: read_all_orders justification (optional)
requirements.detail: Needed only for orders older than 60 days.
requirements.howToPrepare: Describe the app and the feature that needs historical orders.

requirements.label: Emergency developer contact
requirements.detail: An email address and phone number for critical technical issues.
requirements.howToPrepare: Use a monitored team inbox and an on-call number.

requirements.label: App icon
requirements.detail: 1200 x 1200 pixels, JPEG or PNG. App URLs must not contain "Shopify" or "Example".
requirements.howToPrepare: Export your logo at that size.

requirements.label: Mandatory compliance webhooks
requirements.detail: Apps distributed through the App Store must subscribe to compliance webhooks, which are managed in the app configuration TOML.
requirements.howToPrepare: Add the compliance webhook subscriptions to shopify.app.toml and deploy. The individual topics weren't researched here.

requirements.label: App Store registration
requirements.detail: $19 USD, one time per Partner account, paid in Partner Dashboard settings.
requirements.howToPrepare: Have a payment method ready, plus the list of Associated Developer Accounts.

requirements.label: OAuth immediately on install
requirements.detail: The app must authenticate with OAuth before any other step, on install and reinstall, and mustn't ask merchants to type their myshopify.com domain.
requirements.howToPrepare: Start the authorize redirect from your install entry point, using the shop parameter Shopify sends.

limits.whenHit: You need Public distribution, with review, to reach other merchants. Separate custom apps per merchant aren't allowed.
Picking Custom by mistake means creating a new app.

limits.whenHit: Older orders aren't returned until read_all_orders is approved and granted.

blockers.cause: Parameters not sorted, hmac not removed, the wrong secret, or the digest isn't hex-encoded
blockers.fix: Remove hmac, sort the remaining parameters, join them as key=value, run HMAC-SHA256 with the client secret, hex-encode and compare in constant time

blockers.symptom: A spoofed shop domain passes validation
blockers.cause: The regex isn't anchored at the end
The URI doesn't exactly match a configured redirect URL, or the version that added it wasn't released
blockers.fix: Add the exact URI to the app's redirect URLs and release a new version

blockers.symptom: The granted scope is missing read_orders
blockers.cause: Shopify may grant fewer scopes than requested
blockers.fix: Check scope at the callback and send the merchant through authorization again

blockers.symptom: HTTP 200, but order or customer fields are null and the response has an errors entry
blockers.cause: Protected customer data (or a Level 2 field) isn't selected or approved for this app
blockers.fix: Select or request the data under API access requests; on real stores, wait for approval

blockers.symptom: A real merchant store says the app is under review
blockers.fix: Submit for review and wait; meanwhile test only on development stores

blockers.cause: The refresh token expired, was rotated away or is invalid
blockers.fix: Clear the stored pair and send the merchant through authorization again

blockers.symptom: app_access validation error on scopes when releasing or deploying
blockers.cause: read_all_orders was declared before Shopify approved it
blockers.fix: Request approval first, then add the scope

nuances.text: Shopify has three grants. Token exchange (with managed installation, the default for Shopify CLI apps) is the recommended path for embedded apps. The authorization code grant is for apps that run outside the admin, such as a non-embedded backend reading orders. The client credentials grant only works on your own organization's stores. This guide uses the authorization code grant.

There's no global authorize host. Each install goes through the merchant's own {shop}.myshopify.com authorize and token endpoints, and yields a token for that shop only, so store tokens keyed by shop.

App creation and configuration moved to the Dev Dashboard (generally available August 2025). The current protected customer data and read_all_orders pages still describe those requests in the Partner Dashboard under API access requests, and limited visibility is set there too. Expect to use both.
New public apps must send expiring=1. Existing public apps must move to expiring offline tokens for GraphQL Admin API requests by January 1, 2027. Custom and merchant-created apps are exempt.

Refresh tokens rotate. If the refresh response is lost, the old refresh token keeps working until you use the new one, or for up to 30 days after its first use, so retry timeouts with the same token. Don't hard-code a retry window: Shopify's sample comment and prose disagree on it.

In shopify.app.toml, managed installation (the default) requests the declared scopes at install. use_legacy_install_flow = true restores the URL scope parameter, but Shopify doesn't recommend it because installs can end up with different scopes. How the scope parameter interacts with Dev Dashboard version scopes isn't documented.

Limited visibility hides the listing from search but still uses an App Store listing page. Shopify staff confirm that an unlisted multi-store app still needs Public distribution, the full review and the $19 registration.
Even after approval, Shopify may pick an app for a detailed data protection review. That's more likely with many installs, many customer records, more approved fields or long retention.
Custom-distribution apps get Level 1 and Level 2 protected customer data without review, but they can't serve unrelated merchants. That trade-off doesn't help this intent.
Querying only non-customer order fields (such as id and createdAt) avoids the Level 2 gate. Fields like the customer's email trigger it.
